newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares set new high led by blue chip.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares set new high led by blue chip.

text.p: Norwegian shares hit another all-time high on Monday with blue chip stock such as industrial giant Norsk Hydro and forestry group Norske Skogindustrier pulling their weight.
Shipbuilder and engineering group Kvaerner's A share was the most traded of the day, closing 0.79 percent higher at 255 crowns with 161 million crowns worth of shares changing hands.

Kvaerner, at its headquarters in London, released poor nine-month profits but analysts said the market reacted positively to planned cost cuts in the Norwegian group, which last April took over British conglomerate Trafalgar House.
The Total share index, boosted by the strong crown and low interest rates, peaked at 893.28 points in intra-day trade and closed at 891.11, up 0.62 percent on Friday's all-time closing high.
Turnover was a healthy 778 million crowns, down 23 percent from Friday.
Hydro climbed 1.49 percent to close at 306 crowns. Norske Skogindustrier A shares finished 1.67 percent higher at 183 crowns.
